compliance_deadlines: Prohibited practices: 6 months after entry into force (approx. February 2025)
GPAI model obligations: 12 months after entry into force (approx. August 2025)
High-risk AI systems (Annex I): 24 months after entry into force (approx. August 2026)
High-risk AI systems (Annex I, certain sectors): 36 months after entry into force (approx. August 2027)
policy_extraction.penalties_summary: Up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover for violations of prohibited practices; up to €15 million or 3% for other violations; up to €7.5 million or 1.5% for supplying incorrect information. SME/startup penalties scaled proportionately.
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Regulation entered into force 20 days after publication (1 August 2024) with phased applicability. Complements existing EU law on data protection, product safety, consumer protection, and employment. Does not affect GDPR or Directive 2016/680 obligations. European AI Office established within Commission to oversee GPAI models. Member States must designate national competent authorities.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The EU AI Act consistently frames AI governance as necessary to protect fundamental rights, democracy, rule of law, and human dignity as enshrined in the EU Charter. While economic competitiveness and innovation enablement are prominent secondary themes, the primary justification for regulation is the protection of rights and freedoms. The document repeatedly references the Charter of Fundamental Rights, human-centric AI, and protection of natural persons as the core rationale.
